articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft drops 167 patches including a SharePoint zero-day and the deliciously named 'BlueHammer' Windows Defender flaw. Chrome also squeezed in its fourth zero-day of the year because why not make Patch Tuesday extra spicy.

articles.title: Geospatial Intelligence Expert Y. Nithiyanandam on Why the Hormuz Strait is No Longer a Neutral Global Common
articles.summary: CVE-2026-41940 is getting hammered in the wild as threat actor 'Mr_Rot13' deploys Filemanager backdoors on compromised cPanel instances. When your web hosting control panel becomes someone else's control panel, you're having a bad time.

articles.title: Hackers Use AI for Exploit Development, Attack Automation
articles.summary: 'Dirty Frag' joins the Linux privilege escalation hall of fame alongside Copy Fail and Dirty Pipe. Enterprise distros are about to get fragged, and this one might already be seeing limited exploitation in the wild.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: Canvas gets pwned by extortionists, disrupting education nationwide with a ransom demand plastered right on the login page. Nothing says 'back to school' like having your homework held hostage by cybercriminals.

articles.title: OpenAI Launches Daybreak for AI-Powered Vulnerability Detection and Patch Validation
articles.summary: Instructure 'reached an agreement' with ShinyHunters to prevent their 3.65TB Canvas data leak—corporate speak for 'we paid the ransom.' Thousands of schools just learned an expensive lesson about cybersecurity.

articles.title: Canada’s Bill C-22 Is a Repackaged Version of Last Year’s Surveillance Nightmare
articles.summary: Russian military intelligence turns old router vulns into a Microsoft Office token buffet, quietly harvesting auth credentials en masse. Your ancient Linksys just became Moscow's favorite espionage tool.

articles.title: Big Finance Might Be Dooming the SPLC — Even Before Its Day in Court
articles.summary: The DOJ now treats dodging FOIA requests as a criminal offense worthy of arrest and strip searches—peak hypocrisy from an administration that perfected government transparency avoidance. Rules for thee, not for me reaches new heights.

articles.title: EFF to Fourth Circuit: Electronic Device Searches at the Border Require a Warrant
articles.summary: Canada repackages last year's surveillance nightmare as Bill C-22, hoping nobody notices it's still the same digital rights-crushing monster. When your worst sequel makes it to parliament, democracy needs better script writers.

articles.title: EFF Stands in Solidarity With RightsCon and the Global Digital Rights Community
articles.summary: EFF fights for warrant requirements on border device searches in the Fourth Circuit, because apparently 'papers please' now includes your entire digital life. Constitutional rights shouldn't end at customs.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, April 2026 Edition
articles.summary: Scattered Spider's 'Tylerb' pleads guilty to wire fraud and identity theft after a 2022 SMS phishing spree. Another cybercrime legend trades their keyboard for an orange jumpsuit—the circle of lulz continues.
